messages:
oncall-bot: PAGE: hosted-api high latency (p95) — multiple customers reporting errors. Severity: P2. Affected region: eu-west-1. Alerting: cpu/latency/rate.
oncall-bot: Incident channel opened: #incidents. Please ack if you're taking ownership.
mike: ack — I'm on call. collecting initial metrics now, will post timeline.
anya: FYI noticed a correlated jump in batch queue depth ~09:22 UTC, sending trace link: https://traces.internal/r/abc123
sam: can we confirm customer impact? ops-reports show 4 tenants with increased 5xxs between 09:21–09:24 UTC.
laura: digging into p50/p95: baseline p95 ~120ms, jumped to ~1.1s at 09:21 and peaked 1.6s at 09:23 then partial recovery at 09:30. p50 moved from 60ms to 140ms.
mike: sharing quick logs (sanitized):
```
[09:20:58] evict: prefix cache miss spikes
[09:21:05] kvcache_insert_latency_ms p50=2 p95=120 p99=480
[09:21:12] kernel: softirq high on cpu4
[09:21:22] sched: runqueue length spiked on node0
[09:22:07] retried rpc to model-host: context deadline exceeded
```
anya: traced a heavy span chain: model->quantize->copy_kv (heavy memcpy) — span durations: model_infer 300ms, kv_copy 420ms, network 200ms. full spans: https://traces.internal/span/def456
sam: perf counters from the host (09:20–09:25): L1 cache miss rate +32%, page faults +0 (so not user paging), softirq storms on cpu4, context-switch rate x3. Posting perf snippet: `cpu_cycles: +18%`, `cache_misses: +34%`, `minor_faults: 0`
laura: kernel change rolled 09:19 UTC on infra pool nodepool-3 — upstream reverted earlier optimization for softirq handling. rollout id infra-rc-2026-0919. Could be related.
mike: hypothesis 1: kernel change increased softirq handling variance causing runqueue contention and memcpy stalls -> p95 spike. hypothesis 2: a change in batching config caused larger continuous batches increasing KV copy durations.
eng-sre-bot: suggested mitigation: pin affected hosts to previous kernel (infra-rc-2026-0907) and throttle batch size to 1 for the rolling group. Runbook steps: `kubectl patch` -> set BATCH_MAX=1; coordinate with infra for kernel rollback.
anya: applied temporary batching throttle to canary pool at 09:28 UTC — p95 dropped from 1.6s -> 340ms within 2m. Confirming logs show lower kv_copy durations.
sam: customer-impact notes: four tenants saw elevated error rates and timeouts; minimal data loss. CS notified at 09:35 UTC with mitigation steps.
mike: performing kernel rollback dry-run with infra team on one host now. Will post results.
laura: creating timeline snippet for RCA: 09:19 kernel roll 09:21 p95 jump 09:22 kv_copy spike 09:28 throttle applied 09:30 partial recovery 09:40 full mitigation start.
eng-sre-bot: attach for post-incident: raw trace ids [abc123, def456], perf snapshots, kernel package IDs (rc-2026-0919), patched env var used for throttle.
mike: handing off to SRE team for postmortem and deep perf counters — I'll update incident board and add test cases to prevent batch-induced memcpy regressions.
laura: thanks — tagging perf/infra for followup. :thumbsup:
_meta: Generated synthetic incident thread for p95 regression coordination and handoff
